question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-7 \\ 5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ -3{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-7{x}_{2} \\ 5{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2} &=2 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-4 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the first and the second equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{2} &=-2 \\ {x}_{2} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{2}=1$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2} &=-4 \\ -3{x}_{1}+5(1) &=-4 \\ -3{x}_{1} &=-9 \\ {x}_{1} &=3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=1$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=2 \\ (3)-(1) &=2 \\ 2 &=2\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2}=1$, which means

$$
3{a}_{1}+{a}_{2}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(3)+(1)=4.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-12 \\ 28 \\ -22\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3 \\ -3\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-12 \\ 28 \\ -22\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}-2{x}_{2} \\ 3{x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-12 \\ 28 \\ -22\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-12 \\ 28 \\ -22\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=-12 \\ 4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=28 \\ 2{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2} &=-22\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the second and the third equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}_{1} &=6 \\ {x}_{1} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=1$ into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2} &=28 \\ 4(1)+3{x}_{2} &=28 \\ 3{x}_{2} &=24 \\ {x}_{2} &=8\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=8$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2} &=-12 \\ 3(1)-2(8) &=-12 \\ -13 &=-12\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -13 \\ -11\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
.
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 4 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -13 \\ -11\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -13 \\ -11\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -13 \\ -11\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=-13 \\ 4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-11\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Adding the second and the third equations we get

$$
\begin{aligned}8{x}_{1} &=-24 \\ {x}_{1} &=-3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=-3$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ 4(-3)+{x}_{2} &=-11 \\ {x}_{2} &=1 \\ {x}_{2} &=1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=-3$ and ${x}_{2}=1$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2} &=0 \\ (-3)+2(1) &=0 \\ -1 &=0\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a false statement.

So, the system has no solution.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{c}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{c}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\,d=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{c}_{1}+{x}_{2}{c}_{2}=d$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -{x}_{2} \\ -{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=5 \\ {x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Multiplying the third equation by $-1$ and adding the result to the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} &=2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${x}_{1}=2$ into the third equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2} &=3 \\ (2)-{x}_{2} &=3 \\ -{x}_{2} &=1 \\ {x}_{2} &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the first equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}0 &=0 \\ 0 &=0 \\ 0 &=0\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$, which means

$$
2{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}=d.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(2)+(-1)=1.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix},\,b=\begin{bmatrix}-16 \\ 8 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}.
$$

If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b,$ then what is ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}+{x}_{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-16 \\ 8 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-4{x}_{1} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}{x}_{2} \\ 0 \\ 4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-16 \\ 8 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}-4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} \\ 2{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}\end{bmatrix} &=\begin{bmatrix}-16 \\ 8 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-16 \\ 2{x}_{1} &=8 \\ {x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the second equation we get ${x}_{1}=4$.

Substituting ${x}_{1}=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{1}+{x}_{2} &=-16 \\ -4(4)+{x}_{2} &=-16 \\ {x}_{2} &=0 \\ {x}_{2} &=0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=0$ into the third equation to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2} &=4 \\ (4)+4(0) &=4 \\ 4 &=4\end{aligned}
$$

which gives a true statement.

So the solution of the system is ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2}=0$, which means

$$
4{a}_{1}=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=(4)+(0)=4.
$$
